coordination.non_overlap: This receipt excludes memory-store recovery and SOMA state/concurrency findings already integrated elsewhere; it focuses on process/service recovery loops, cancellation reachability, packaging/fresh-install boot, noninteractive install observability, seed-state boot and deployment topology drift.

historical_units.focus: agent cancellation reachability and timeout bounding
PyInstaller bundle/startup failure, self-bootstrap fork-loop risk, clean-VM install proof
needrestart interactive hang, hidden installer errors, clean-VM deployment validation
seed databases and deployment-time restart/shutdown race findings

findings.claim: ASRS created a positive feedback loop by counting systemd lifecycle errors caused by its own rollback/restart actions as fresh application errors. The resulting loop was restart -> error log -> error detection -> more restart until lifecycle messages were excluded from the error counter.
findings.implication: Recovery observability must distinguish exogenous failure evidence from telemetry generated by the recovery action itself. Recovery-generated observations need causal provenance and anti-retrigger semantics.
findings.next_test: Inject one service failure, execute recovery, and feed recovery-generated lifecycle/error events back into monitoring. Assert exactly one bounded recovery episode unless independent post-recovery evidence fails validation.

findings.claim: Agent cancellation existed as persistent state manipulation but did not cancel the actually running AgentLoop because the UI instantiated a different loop object. The repair stored a reference to the live loop, added a cancellation flag checked at iteration and LLM-call boundaries, and shortened long blocking inference calls with bounded retries.
findings.implication: Cancellation is a causal-control-path property, not a database flag. H1/H2/H3 must prove that cancel/stop reaches the live execution authority within bounded latency and leaves a replayable terminal state.
findings.next_test: Start a deliberately slow multi-step task, request cancel during model wait and during tool execution, measure cancel-to-quiescence latency, verify no subsequent capability commits, and replay the cancellation receipt.

findings.claim: Fresh Ubuntu deployment exposed hidden environment assumptions: wrong package naming, missing zstd, missing PYTHONPATH for services and absence of a user systemd bus. These defects were found only when the installer was exercised in an Ubuntu 24.04 systemd-nspawn environment.
findings.implication: A source-tree run on the development machine is insufficient deployment proof. Clay 0.1 needs clean-environment boot tests with explicit environment, dependency and service/runtime assumptions.
findings.next_test: Build from a frozen source/ref into a clean Ubuntu reference environment with empty HOME/cache, verify all required dependencies/configuration are generated from declared inputs, then repeat with missing optional user bus and CPU-only hardware.

findings.claim: A standalone installer binary crashed because its TUI dependency was not fully bundled; its fallback bootstrap could also recurse/fork-loop when the frozen binary attempted to pip-install into itself. After correcting bundle collection and bootstrap mode detection, the repository reports a clean Ubuntu 24.04 VM run with 14/14 installer steps, 13 services running and zero failures.
findings.implication: Packaging is part of executable system correctness. Self-bootstrap paths must be mode-aware, terminating and idempotent; successful source execution cannot substitute for packaged-artifact boot proof.
findings.next_test: Run packaged artifact in a clean environment with a deliberately missing optional dependency and an incomplete prior install directory; require bounded fail/repair behavior without recursion and verify deterministic recovery or explicit refusal.

findings.claim: Ubuntu needrestart prompts combined with sudo environment stripping, quiet apt flags and stderr suppression made the installer appear frozen. The repair made package operations noninteractive, preserved environment through sudo and exposed progress/errors; the repository reports a later clean 8GB CPU-only Ubuntu VM installation completing all 14 steps with 27 services running.
findings.implication: Headless automation must make blocking state observable. Silence is not robustness: operations need explicit progress/timeout/error receipts and classification of fatal vs optional failures.
findings.next_test: Inject interactive package prompt, stalled network step and optional package failure. Harness must surface current phase and bounded timeout, distinguish optional degradation from fatal boot failure, and never hang indefinitely.

findings.claim: Later deployment explicitly shipped seed databases and copied each seed only when the target database did not already exist, while preserving runtime databases from version control. This demonstrates that historically valid FRANK boot depended on a distinction between code, schema/seed state and accumulated live state.
findings.implication: Reference Harness boot must declare and hash initial cognitive/state substrate separately from code/runtime. Fresh boot, upgrade boot and restore boot are different acceptance cases and must not overwrite accumulated state with seeds.
findings.next_test: Three-way boot matrix: blank fresh install receives canonical seed state; upgrade preserves mutated state while applying compatible migrations; restore reproduces a snapshot. Compare hashes, identities and transition receipts.

findings.claim: The historical deployment surface changed rapidly: the repository reports clean installs with 13 services, later 27 services, and another installer revision describing 36 services; current Clay 0.1 explicitly targets a one-module/binary FRANK stage. Therefore raw service count is not a stable behavioral acceptance invariant across architecture generations.
findings.implication: Harness should specify capability/state-transition invariants and causal behavior, not encode a historical process/service count. Service collapse is allowed if the behavioral contracts survive.
findings.next_test: Run the same behavioral/recovery acceptance suite against H1 reference topology, H2 ClayCode topology and H3 one-module topology; compare external semantics rather than process count.

findings.claim: A deployment audit found a Thalamus singleton shutdown race and a neural-immune supervisor TOCTOU race in restart requests in addition to wrong service port mappings. These show that restart authority and shared singleton lifecycle were recurrent failure points in the multi-service architecture.
findings.implication: Even if H3 removes many process boundaries, lifecycle transitions need single authoritative ownership, idempotent stop/start and compare-before-commit semantics. Multi-service H1 should specifically stress TOCTOU/restart races.
findings.next_test: Concurrent stop/restart/health-check adversary with reordered events and duplicate restart requests; require exactly-once logical lifecycle transitions and no stale owner writes.

earned_work_candidates.validation: Recovery-self-trigger, live-cancel and concurrent-lifecycle fixtures must fail against historical-style mechanisms and pass against current implementations.
Clean-environment, packaging, noninteractive, fresh/upgrade/restore and cross-topology acceptance matrix on current runtime.

branch_feedback.harness: Add recovery self-observation suppression, live cancel reachability, clean-environment packaging, noninteractive hang, seed/upgrade/restore boot and concurrent lifecycle fixtures. Validate H1/H2/H3 by behavior, not service count.
branch_feedback.frank: Treat recovery and cancellation as causal control paths with explicit authority and replay; separate code boot from initial/accumulated state boot.
branch_feedback.claycode: Model lifecycle/cancel/recovery/boot transitions explicitly enough to produce deterministic receipts and idempotent replay; do not inherit historical systemd topology as semantics.
branch_feedback.unifieddb: Boot identity needs seed/schema/live-state provenance and non-destructive upgrade/restore semantics.
branch_feedback.claygraph: Preserve seed/live-state ancestry and recovery-event provenance so restore/replay cannot silently fabricate independent state.
branch_feedback.emergenz: Recovery-loop finding is a concrete self-coupling failure: feedback generated by an intervention can amplify itself unless causal provenance separates intervention effects from exogenous evidence.
branch_feedback.clay: Historical packaging/deployment tests are reusable acceptance scaffolding; current one-module target must still pass clean boot/recovery semantics.

progress_accounting.reason: History-aware exact manifest and Drive archive internals remain unfrozen; this valid semantic shard cannot manufacture exact coverage.
